store.0: I'm a fourth-year computer science major, 21, almost 22, and my hobbies keep me sane. I love coding, but I need breaks to come back to it with a fresh perspective.
store.1: Sailing is a unique hobby among my friends. I grew up near a marina and was hooked after feeling the rush of wind against the sails. I keep up with it in college by renting boats at a student rate and spending hours on the water. It gives me a sense of freedom and appeals to my problem-solving side.
store.2: I'm a fan of both PC and console games, but spend more time on PC. I enjoy co-op survival games and fast-paced shooters. Gaming is a social thing and a mental challenge for me. I've also dabbled in game development using Unity and Unreal Engine, and want to explore it more deeply if time permits.
store.3: I schedule my hobbies like I schedule study time to keep a healthy balance. Every Sunday, I plan out my week and fit in activities like gym time, sailing, gaming, and reading.
store.4: I like combining hobbies. For example, I've had a day where we sailed in the morning, grabbed lunch, and then played video games in the evening. I love how each hobby demands teamwork, attention to detail, and problem-solving.
store.5: It can be stressful with a heavy course load, but I find ways to fit in my hobbies in small increments. I might not have hours to read, sail, or game, but I can read one chapter, sail once a month, or play a quick match.
store.6: My hobbies give me something to talk about outside of coding. They range from reading to sailing, weightlifting to co-op games. It makes life interesting and shows a different side of me.
